Two snapshot files share revision r0051: 20260815T141330Z-r0051-MNT-20260815T141330Z.json and 20260815T232146Z-r0051.json; both predate 2026-08-31 and are outside this scan's change window.
inferences: The scanned-watermark bookkeeping is write-once-on-attempt rather than write-on-coverage: a source is stamped scanned when a worker finishes, not when its declared inputs were actually read. Because due-source selection consumes only last_scanned_at, an input that is missing or that failed to fetch is not merely missed once — it is guaranteed to stay missed, since nothing schedules a retry and nothing marks the source as partially covered.

The recurrence is proven by a full maintenance cycle elapsing without repair: discovery-06 reported the nonexistent findings/ path on 2026-08-31 both as an explicit risk and as a note persisted into sources.json, and the controller nonetheless re-issued the identical path list in the 2026-09-07 plan and advanced the watermark. A defect recorded into a free-text field is not routed to any repair path.

This is a general AI-development mechanism, not merely a quirk of this maintenance controller: any agent evidence-collection loop that tracks freshness with a per-source timestamp, and records fetch failures as prose rather than as structured coverage state, will silently overstate its own coverage and converge on a stable blind spot.

The practical response is not derivable from any of the 193 catalogued problems: advance the freshness watermark per declared input rather than per source, record fetch outcome as a structured status, and treat a missing or failed input as a due item on the next cycle instead of as a completed one.

The third consecutive authority_base.reachable false is confirming evidence for the already-catalogued P-20260831-FB4523EC rather than a new problem; it does strengthen that entry from 2-of-3 to 3-of-4 runs and is worth attaching as evidence.

Absence of token/time budgets and actuals again makes the 'unexplained time or token loss' query theme unevidenceable from local data; consistent with the prior scout, this stays covered by G22/K06/K11 and warrants no new entry.

The 23-day-old unowned decision package and the fixed per-run action caps remain oversight-bandwidth symptoms already carried by J03/J15/G14; the duplicate r0051 snapshot revision is the A03/A14 duplicated-counter mechanism and is out of window.

risks: The evidence is single-project: the mechanism is observed in this maintenance controller's own discovery loop over two cycles, not across independent tools. The controller should judge whether it generalizes to AI development at large before promoting it, as it did for P-20260831-FB4523EC.

C01 (necessary files cannot be retrieved, work proceeds on incomplete premises) and D08 (reference targets circular/missing/stale) are the nearest catalog neighbours; if the controller reads the mechanism as merely 'a missing input', it collapses into those. The distinguishing element is the freshness-watermark bookkeeping that converts a one-time miss into a permanent, self-concealing blind spot.

Because the findings/ path has never existed, it is possible it was aspirational rather than a regression; the problem is then the unreconciled declaration plus the success stamp, not a lost data feed.
The 2026-09-07 run artifacts are untracked and the run is still in-flight, so this scan's inputs may change before the run is committed.

records.summary: The maintenance controller's discovery loop stamps each source with a single last_scanned_at watermark when a worker finishes, not when the source's declared inputs were actually read. In catalog/sources.json the local-project-evidence source declares two paths, one of which ('.ai-intelligence/ai-development/findings') does not exist and never has, yet its watermark was advanced to 2026-08-31T19:16:58Z and it was counted among 'sources_scanned: 6' in runs/MNT-20260831T190559Z/metrics.json. The same shape appears in two sibling sources whose last_result.notes record an arXiv HTTP 400 with ACM/IEEE unindexed, and MITRE ATLAS coverage unverified, while carrying identical fully-scanned watermarks. Because due-source selection and maintenance-policy.json cadence read only the watermark, and because the failure is preserved solely as prose in last_result.notes with no structured per-input coverage field, nothing schedules a retry: the gap is not merely missed once but guaranteed to stay missed. The recurrence is demonstrated across a full cycle -- runs/MNT-20260831T190559Z/workers/discovery-06.json reported the nonexistent path as both a fact and a risk, and MNT-20260907T190654Z-maintain.json nonetheless re-issued the identical path list to discovery-04 and re-advanced the watermark. The self-concealing property is what distinguishes this from C01 and D08: coverage is overstated by the very record that is supposed to reveal it.
